biography: Mike Alexander's journey into the heart of American stock car racing began not on the asphalt, but on the dusty dirt tracks of rural Oklahoma. Growing up, his weekends were spent watching his father, a local legend, wrestle a beat-up Chevy around the oval. At 16, after years of begging, Mike finally got his chance. His raw talent was undeniable, even if his consistency was questionable. He won his first amateur race in a borrowed car, a victory fueled by adrenaline and a healthy dose of youthful recklessness. The transition to Stock USA Gen1 was a steep learning curve, marked by spectacular crashes and occasional flashes of brilliance. He landed a spot with a smaller team, 'Dust Devil Racing,' but sponsorship woes forced them to shutter. Now, at 24, Mike's with 'American Thunder,' a team willing to gamble on his potential. He knows this is his shot to prove he's more than just a flash in the pan, and he's ready to take it.
drivingStyle: Mike's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward approach. He's known for late-braking maneuvers and aggressive corner entries, often pushing his car to the absolute limit. He isn't the most patient driver, which can lead to impulsive decisions on track. Tire management is his biggest weakness, as he tends to overdrive the car early in a stint, sacrificing long-run pace for immediate gains. When under pressure, he becomes even more erratic, making both spectacular passes and costly mistakes.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, regardless of the weather.
Listens to classic rock at full volume right before every race to 'get the blood pumping'.
Has a pre-race ritual of drawing a small lightning bolt on his steering wheel with a permanent marker.
famousQuote: "I'd rather crash trying to win than cruise around for second place. That's not racing, that's just participating."
careerHighlight: Winning the 'Oklahoma Showdown' in his first year of amateur racing, beating seasoned veterans and proving his natural talent.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 'Daytona Duel' in his first major Stock USA Gen1 race, destroying his car and severely damaging his confidence.
